walkthroughs: A composition-only differential can be unchanged while CPU per fixed work doubles; the existing workflow requires raw totals and the workload denominator.
Changing only completed work from 1,000 to 2,000 makes the same doubling compatible with unchanged CPU per operation; an application optimization is not automatically warranted.
Missing raw/event provenance permits a bounded description rather than invention of units or a blanket refusal.
A changed child can coexist with a white parent under self-delta coloring; a zero-width removed path can be absent from the candidate-width graph.
behavioralEvaluations.classification: Existing converter fixture executed technically; actor behavior and skill effectiveness were not evaluated. The two cases below are development cases, not holdouts.

sources.supports: Second-profile width basis, reversed-input plus negate complement, direct folded comparison columns and total normalization.
Self-delta coloring, width pruning, sign reversal, distinct --reverse/--inverted semantics and search-overlap handling. Actual SVG controls were generated.
Original differential methodology and normalization/width limitations.
Conventional geometry, cumulative search, alternate palettes and flame-chart versus aggregated flame-graph distinction.
Event-specific interval units, --total versus sample counts, frame include/exclude filtering and orthogonal reversed/inverted views.
Initial method instrumentation may trigger deoptimization; preserved as a hypothesis requiring actual settings/lifecycle evidence.
Application-dependent capture overhead and Heap Statistics triggering old collections. The skill appropriately avoids treating these effects as universal merely because a JFR file exists.

limitations: No behavioral actor runs, matched original/revised comparison or measured skill gain.
No application, JDK or production profiler was run. Converter validation uses synthetic folded stacks and verifies only the pinned classic FlameGraph scripts.
The generated SVGs were checked through their emitted frame/title/color data, not through interactive browser testing.
async-profiler and JFR version-sensitive statements were checked in primary sources; their runtime implementations were not exercised.
No executable Java snippet was added or changed; compilation is not applicable. Existing JFR diagnostic command sketches were read, not executed.
No-change means this scoped review found no supported gap, not proof that every future interpretation will be correct.
